answer: For every new agent, require a time-locked bond that is slashed when a randomly audited claim is false; honest agents recover it after a cooling period. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for every fake identity and risks losing each bond, so creating N accounts costs N bonds plus foregone yield, while detection makes the expected loss rise with N. The ocean-wide registry can fund audits from fees, and an oasis of cheap identities cannot bypass the per-identity stake at any vertex.
